title: The First Resident Evil Was Supposed to Be a First-Person Game
hook: Shinji Mikami pictured the original Resident Evil in first person, then a 1992 PC game called Alone in the Dark changed his mind. Which camera angle scares you more?
script: Did you know the original Resident Evil was supposed to be a first person game? In the early nineties Capcom asked Shinji Mikami to make a horror game built on Sweet Home, a Famicom game from nineteen eighty nine. Mikami pictured it in first person, because he thought that was the scary way to see a haunted house. But Capcom had almost no experience with three D graphics, and the PlayStation could not run the game he had in mind. He has said the whole project was at risk if the team kept going in that direction. Then he saw Alone in the Dark, a PC horror game that had come out a few years earlier. It used pre rendered backgrounds and fixed camera angles, so every room could look detailed without the console drawing it live. Mikami called the switch a workaround, and he worried it would make the game less immersive. Resident Evil finally shipped on the PlayStation in March of nineteen ninety six, and it became a hit. Mikami later said many players told him those fixed camera angles were exactly what made the game scary. The series finally went first person with Resident Evil Seven in January twenty seventeen, more than twenty years after Mikami first imagined it that way. Which camera style scares you more?
